source_reachability:
I fetched every URL myself with curl -A "Mokaair-editorial" (no personal data in any request). Statuses I saw on 2026-09-16:

BLOCKED — https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/ = HTTP 403 (9,812-byte Cloudflare block body), and HTTP 403 again via WebFetch, i.e. a second egress path. Also 403: /index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/index.txt, /news/, /llms.txt, and the official zh-Hant translation /zh-Hant/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/. cdn.openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai.html = 404. So source #1 in the researcher's sources[] is NOT reachable from this container; its body exists in the record only through the Wayback captures.

REACHABLE, REAL CONTENT —
https://openai.com/news/rss.xml = 200, 726,611 B, 1,195 <item>, newest pubDate Wed, 16 Sep 2026 16:00:00 GMT (live, not dead, not an Access-Denied body). Carries the funding item verbatim.
https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ = 200, 1,238,668 B, 261 <url>, contains <loc>https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/</loc> + <lastmod>2026-08-13T23:42:20.362Z</lastmod> + a zh-Hant hreflang alternate.
https://openai.com/sitemap.xml = 200 (3,414 B); https://openai.com/robots.txt = 200 (98 B).
https://web.archive.org/web/20260915092422/https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/ = 200, 385,815 B — a genuine capture of OpenAI's page, not a challenge page; og:title and og:description are byte-identical to the live RSS I pulled straight from openai.com.
https://web.archive.org/web/20260405075032/... = 200, 321,567 B, same og:title/og:description/byline, contains $122 billion and 852.
https://group.softbank/en/news/press/20260227 = 200 (206,950 B); /20260327 = 200 (193,644 B); /20260401_0 = 200 (192,031 B); /20260701 = 200 (193,923 B) — all render the full press-release body to curl.
https://group.softbank/en/news/press = 200 (269,019 B); the listing confirms all four dated paths as real hrefs, spans 2026-02-13 to 2026-09-09, and shows no OpenAI item after 2026-07-01.
https://press.aboutamazon.com/2026/2/openai-and-amazon-announce-strategic-partnership = 200 (155,750 B), rel=canonical equals that URL, datePublished 2026-02-27T13:30:00Z, full body plus both executive quotes.
https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/releases.xml = 200 (68,371 B) but only 4 items, oldest 2026-09-01 — it cannot reach March 2026, which independently supports excluding any NVIDIA amount.

My full record: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-travel-scanner/7f63d65a-c509-5a16-8b56-4ffddc3bb57b/scratchpad/research/ai-news-openai-funding-20260331.factcheck.json (written under .factcheck.json so the researcher's own ai-news-openai-funding-20260331.json is not overwritten).

refuted.fact: verified_facts[20]: "The body text of the official page is unchanged ... 26 body paragraphs, identical wording"
refuted.why:
The substance is correct — I ran my own

-level diff of the 2026-04-05 and 2026-09-15 captures and the article text is identical, with only nav chrome and the three "Keep reading" cards differing (April: Apr 2 / Mar 24 / Mar 19 2026; September: Sep 9 / Sep 8 / Sep 8 2026). But the count is wrong. The Sept capture has 28

elements, of which 1 is a nav-class fragment and 3 are Keep-reading cards, leaving 24 article paragraphs (and those 24 already include the 4 section headings "Deep conviction across global capital", "Leadership across consumer and enterprise", "Compute is a strategic advantage", "Building an AI superapp"). There is no reading of the markup that yields 26.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[7]: "It also claims it is growing revenue four times faster than Alphabet and Meta did."
refuted.why: The page actually says: "At this stage, we are growing revenue four times faster than the companies who defined the Internet and mobile eras, including Alphabet and Meta." Alphabet and Meta are given as examples inside a broader comparison set, not as the benchmark. As worded the researcher's fact narrows OpenAI's claim into a head-to-head that OpenAI did not make, and the researcher's own verbatim_quote does not cover that sentence at all — it stops before it.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[9]: "OpenAI lists the other participating institutions as Altimeter, Appaloosa LP, ARK Invest, ..."
unsupported.why: All 19 names match the page exactly — I checked each one. But the page says "There was also significant participation from a diverse set of global institutions including ...". "Including" makes the list explicitly non-exhaustive, so "lists the other participating institutions as" is not supported. Also verbatim_quote is empty for this fact, which is the one place a checker most needs it.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[12]: "supported by a syndicate of JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Mizuho, Royal Bank of Canada, SMBC, UBS, HSBC and Santander"
unsupported.why: The page says "The facility is supported by a global syndicate including JPMorgan Chase, ...". Same non-exhaustive problem, and the researcher's quote elides the sentence with "..." so the omission is invisible. The 11 names and the ~$4.7bn and "remains undrawn at close" are all confirmed.

This is the biggest decision in the record and I cannot confirm it. I independently re-verified that openai.com/index/* is 403 on two different egress paths, and that the Wayback captures are authentic (og:description byte-identical to the RSS I pulled live from openai.com; byline matches the RSS pubDate; my own April-vs-September diff shows no revision). Nothing is fabricated. But the BRIEF is explicit: 「查到的事實如果只存在於被擋的頁面後面，那就不寫」. Every user-facing body number — 900M weekly users, 50M subscribers, $2B/month, $4.7bn revolver, $3bn from individual investors, the superapp, the $852bn post-money — exists in this record only via web.archive.org. This needs a human sign-off, not a researcher self-grade. The researcher does offer the downgrade path in its own notes, which is to its credit.

unsupported.fact: sources[] (4 entries) vs the facts that depend on them
unsupported.why: facts[23] cites https://group.softbank/en/news/press/20260327 (bridge facility) and facts[25] cites https://group.softbank/en/news/press/20260701 (second tranche); neither URL is in sources[]. The BRIEF caps sources at 4 and requires every date/figure to point at a source's original text. If the article uses the bridge facility or the July tranche, the source list has to be rebuilt — most likely by dropping the 2026-04-01 release in favour of the 2026-02-27 one, which already contains the whole tranche table.

Already stale a few hours later: I count 1,195 items and 35 September items, and the newest item is now "Helping older adults use AI in everyday life" (Wed, 16 Sep 2026 16:00:00 GMT), not "Reimagining advertising with AI" (13:00 GMT). Harmless for the article, but the corrections_to_candidate_list entry will be wrong the moment anyone re-runs it.

additional_findings: HIGH VALUE, MISSED, and it partly rescues the archive problem: SoftBank's 2026-02-27 release states the round's PRE-MONEY valuation as USD 730 billion. 730 + 122 = 852. So OpenAI's $852bn post-money is corroborated by a second first-party source that is NOT behind any block — and the $122bn itself appears in OpenAI's own RSS description, which I fetched directly from openai.com. The two headline numbers therefore do not depend on Wayback at all. The researcher read that page and did not notice.

MISSED, and it bears directly on the IPO section: SoftBank 2026-02-27 states the securities acquired are "Preferred Shares (automatically convertible into common shares of OpenAI upon an IPO or related listing transaction)". The researcher's not_said says OpenAI never mentions an IPO — true of OpenAI's post, but a first-party listing hook does exist in the SoftBank filing.

MISSED from SoftBank 2026-02-27: SBG had already invested an aggregate USD 34.6 billion via SoftBank Vision Fund 2 since September 2024 (34.6 + 30.0 = 64.6, matching the cumulative figure that was recorded); SBG board resolution 2026-02-20 (Japan time); consideration financed initially through bridge loans; LTV policy below 25% normally and 35% in emergency; OpenAI Group PBC founded November 2018, reorganized into a PBC October 2025, Sam Altman CEO, San Francisco; FVTPL fair-value accounting; quotes from Masayoshi Son and Sam Altman.

MISSED: the acceleration-on-listing footnote is in the 2026-02-27 release as well ("*4 Closing dates may be subject to acceleration in the event of a public listing of OpenAI shares"), not only in the 2026-07-01 release where the researcher put it.

MISSED from SoftBank 2026-03-27: the bridge facility lenders are JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and MUFG Bank; maturity 2027-03-25; collateral None; repayable in stages. Note four of those banks also sit in OpenAI's own revolver syndicate — a genuinely interesting first-party overlap.

MISSED from Amazon 2026-02-27: OpenAI and Amazon will develop customized models to power Amazon's customer-facing applications; the Trainium commitment spans Trainium3 and Trainium4; Trainium4 is "expected to begin delivery in 2027"; the Stateful Runtime Environment was "expected to launch in the next few months" as of that date. All four are dated, checkable and unrecorded.

MISSED from OpenAI's own post — the paragraph on what the money has already produced: "We recently launched GPT-5.4, our most capable model yet, with meaningful gains in intelligence and workflow performance. We expanded Codex into a flagship coding agent. We pushed forward on memory, search, personalization, and multimodal interaction. We also expanded into areas like health, scientific discovery, and commerce." Also dropped: "and with this round we are deepening that partnership as we scale" from the Nvidia paragraph.

CHARACTER TRAP the researcher did not flag, and the BRIEF warns about exactly this: the page writes GPT‑5.4 with U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN in both occurrences. Anyone grepping the capture with an ASCII hyphen will get zero hits.

ARK: the only first-party page I found on ark-funds.com concerns ARK Venture Fund (ARKVX), a closed-end interval fund holding private companies — not an ETF. That is a lead, not a confirmation. The researcher's exclusion is correct and should stand; if ARK is mentioned at all it must stay at "OpenAI 表示" level with no ticker.

NVIDIA exclusion independently re-confirmed: nvidianews.nvidia.com/releases.xml now holds only 4 items reaching back to 2026-09-01 (the researcher said 2026-08-31 — it has rolled further forward), and a domain-restricted search of nvidianews / blogs.nvidia / investor.nvidia surfaces only the September 2025 10-gigawatt partnership. No NVIDIA amount may be written.

"Third tranche has not yet occurred as of 2026-09-16" holds: I fetched the SoftBank press listing (200), which runs through 2026-09-09 and contains no third-tranche and no acceleration release after 2026-07-01.

Overall: this is the cleanest researcher record I have checked. No invented URL, no guessed pcode-style identifier, no news outlet or aggregator standing in for a first-party page, no announcement/publication/effective date conflated, and every vendor metric already carries is_vendor_claim true. All four sources[] URLs are attested first-party — the trailing-slash canonical by OpenAI's own sitemap <loc>, the no-slash form by the RSS guid, the four SoftBank paths by real hrefs on group.softbank/en/news/press, the Amazon URL by its own rel=canonical. The fixes needed are two wording corrections, one wrong paragraph count, a rebuilt sources[] array, and a human decision on the Wayback dependency.
